chunks: Muhammad ibn Ahmad ibn Yahya narrated from Bunan ibn Muhammad from Musa ibn al-Qasim from Ali ibn Ja'far from his brother Musa ibn Ja'far (peace be upon him) who said:
I asked him about a woman who marries on top of her paternal aunt and maternal aunt. He said: There is no harm.
And he said: Marry the paternal aunt and the maternal aunt upon the daughter of the brother and the daughter of the sister.
And do not marry the daughter of the brother and the sister upon the paternal aunt and the maternal aunt, except with their consent.

Then whoever does that, his marriage is invalid. With the understanding that the two reports can bear another meaning, which is that we interpret them as a form of taqiyya (prudent dissimulation), because all of the Sunnis differ with us in this matter and claim that this is a matter of consensus, and this is its ruling: taqiyya applies to it.

key_terms.تَقِيَّة: Taqiyya (prudent dissimulation or concealment of belief/ruling due to fear or difference with majority)

ai.seo_question: Is it permissible to marry an aunt and her niece at the same time in Shia Islam?
ai.summary: This hadith from al-Isfahani clarifies the Shia ruling on simultaneous marriage to a woman and her aunt, distinguishing it from the prohibition of sisters by requiring the aunt's consent for the latter case. The jurist highlights that this specific ruling may be an instance of *taqiyya* (dissimulation), as the Sunni majority considers simultaneous marriage to an aunt and niece to be invalid based on consensus (*ijma*), whereas Shia jurisprudence permits it under certain conditions.
